d01.prompt: Write a 650-word essay for a technology-policy newsletter arguing that a device is not fully owned when its maker can disable features after sale. The readers already follow digital-rights issues. Use no headline or signoff.

d02.prompt: Write a 650-word essay for workers and labour organisers about software that changes shifts at short notice. Explain why unpredictability is a form of control, not only an inconvenience. Use no headline or signoff.

d03.prompt: Write a 650-word essay for a general civil-liberties audience arguing that digital access to public court records should not depend on expensive private databases. Use no headline or signoff.

d04.prompt: Write a 650-word essay for parents and privacy advocates about why an online age-checking system can become identity infrastructure even when a law describes it as a narrow safety measure. Use no headline or signoff.

d05.prompt: Write a 700-word blog post for software developers. Title: Choice screens are not market choice. Cover: who selects the listed options; how defaults shape behaviour; why nominal choice can preserve gatekeeper power; and what a meaningful remedy would change. Keep the title.

d06.prompt: Write a 700-word blog post for owners of connected home devices. Title: The server was part of the appliance. Cover: a vendor closing its cloud service; which features stop working; why the shutdown changes the original bargain; and what local operation would protect. Keep the title.

d07.prompt: Write a 700-word blog post for independent repair shops. Title: A manual is a tool. Cover: service information withheld as intellectual property; the cost to small shops; the link between documentation and parts pairing; and a practical disclosure rule. Keep the title.

d08.prompt: Write a 300-word reply to a longtime reader whose public library ebook vanished during a loan after the publisher withdrew it. The reader asks whether this is just the digital version of returning a book. Answer directly and informally, but treat the question seriously.

d09.prompt: Write a 300-word reply to a colleague at a small nonprofit who asks whether they should use an AI service to summarise confidential intake notes. They need a practical answer for a meeting tomorrow. Be direct, collegial, and specific about the decision.

d10.prompt: Write a 300-word reply to an independent app developer who has been told to add age assurance but cannot afford a specialist vendor. The developer asks whether collecting identity documents is the only safe option. Answer for a technically informed peer.
